messages:
marta: seeing a spike of KV cache allocations on prod-r-12 during a long-chat load, caused an OOM and a node restart. attaching rough timeline and logs, need quick mitigation.

alex: thanks, can you paste the node logs? curious if this coincided with a kernel switch or a batch-size spike.

marta: pasted snippets below. note: at 11:02 we routed traffic to v2-kernel (quantized fallback) for a canary, then at 11:05 memory started climbing and compaction didn't keep up.
```
[11:04:58] kv_alloc: slab 0x7f.. size 3.2G -> total_kv 27.8G
[11:05:03] kv_compact: started compaction but scanned 12 segments, freed 0.3G
[11:05:17] oom-killer: process runtime_worker killed by OOM
```

priya: odd — v2-kernel should be lower memory. did we switch kernel selection heuristics at the same time? maybe kernel selected fp16 path for some layers and that enabled larger temp buffers.

alex: quick repro note: the sampler for kernel selection uses the last N seq lengths to pick kernels. if the moving window is skewed by a few long contexts, it can pick a kernel with higher scratch requirements. that's a bug we've seen in perf lab.

sam: oom-bot reported: "oom_detected prod-r-12 11:05 runtime_worker" and then deploy-bot restarted the pod. no user-facing errors yet but some requests timed out.

oom-bot: [alert] automatic restart triggered for pod prod-r-12 due to OOM at 11:05:17. Pod restarted at 11:05:22.

jess: immediate mitigation options: 1) route traffic away from prod-r-12 (already draining), 2) force kernel selection to safe path, 3) temporarily enable aggressive KV eviction for long contexts. which do we prefer?

marta: do 2 + 3 ASAP. traffic drain in flight is already happening. we need to avoid another restart while we debug.

alex: I'll flip kernel heuristic to prefer low-scratch kernels for the next 15m: 
```
curl -XPOST https://ops/api/kernels/select?mode=conservative -d '{"ttl":900}'
```

priya: I'll push a hotpatch to KV manager to make prefix-eviction more aggressive for sequences > 8k tokens: decrement reuse score by 0.5 and faster async evict loop. small change, low risk.

sam: I'll add a temporary SLO throttle rule: drop requests with seq_len > 12k for the next 30m to prevent compaction chasing tail growth.

jess: flagging a postmortem ticket and scheduling a quick runbook update. also we should consider a graceful fallback route (serve a truncated context + notice) instead of full OOM.

marta: for the postmortem let's capture: kernel-selection window bias, KV compaction latency under sustained long-context traffic, and batch-size distribution when this happened.

alex: follow-up experiment ideas: 1) reduce kernel selection window from 200 -> 50 samples to react faster, 2) add a scratch-budget check to kernel_selector that rejects kernels exceeding per-request scratch cap, 3) simulate mixed long/short context workload in perf lab to reproduce.

priya: took the hotpatch and applied to prod-r-12, eviction loop now triggered every 200ms instead of 1s for large prefixes. watching metrics.

oom-bot: [info] kv_evictions increased on prod-r-12 at 11:12.

marta: memory growth flattened after the patches. we avoided a second restart. good call.

sam: action items: 
- alex: implement scratch-budget gate in kernel selector (P0).
- priya: land KV eviction tuning as a config flag and roll across fleet (P0).
- jess: update runbook with fallback to truncated-context responses + user notice (P1).
- marta: collect traces and profile the compaction loop to find hotspots (P0).

alex: quick patch for scratch-budget looks like: 
```
if kernel.scratch_bytes > request.scratch_budget:
  skip_kernel(kernel)
```
I'll open PR now.

priya: PR for eviction tuning: https://git/repo/pull/1234 (small config + unit test).

marta: I'll attach heap profiles and compaction traces in the ticket.

jess: thanks everyone. keep the thread updated if any regressions or new OOMs. :thumbsup:

sam: noting a follow-up: consider a soft-fallback where if compaction can't keep up, we serve from a quantized-small model (lower KV footprint) and mark requests with a telemetry flag so clients can surface degraded quality.

marta: agreed — mapping to roadmap item for graceful fallback to smaller model (tracking id: FWB-42).

alex: PR opened for kernel gate: https://git/repo/pull/1250 (tests + perf run).

priya: rolling eviction tuning to 20% of fleet now, will monitor for false-evicts.

oom-bot: [resolved] OOM incident resolved for prod-r-12 at 11:18.

marta: closing loop: no further OOMs in last 45m. will write up the postmortem and link here.
